     6	/// SQL statements are represented as an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The
     7	/// statement is the root node of this tree, and describes the syntactic
     8	/// structure of a SQL statement. It is built from a raw SQL string by the
     9	/// parser, and passed on to the planner which validates it and builds an
    10	/// execution plan from it.
    11	#[derive(Debug)]
    12	pub enum Statement {

    14	    Begin {
    15	        /// READ ONLY: if true, begin a read-only transaction.
    16	        read_only: bool,
    17	        /// AS OF: if given, the MVCC version to read at.
    18	        as_of: Option<u64>,
    19	    },
    20	    /// COMMIT: commits a transaction.
    21	    Commit,
    22	    /// ROLLBACK: rolls back a transaction.
    23	    Rollback,

   147	/// SQL expressions, e.g. `a + 7 > b`. Can be nested.
   148	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, Hash, PartialEq)]
   149	pub enum Expression {
   150	    /// All columns, i.e. *.
   151	    All,
   152	    /// A column reference, optionally qualified with a table name.
   153	    Column(Option<String>, String),
   154	    /// A literal value.
   155	    Literal(Literal),
   156	    /// A function call (name and parameters).
   157	    Function(String, Vec<Expression>),

   162	/// Expression literal values.
   163	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
   164	pub enum Literal {
   165	    Null,
   166	    Boolean(bool),
   167	    Integer(i64),
   168	    Float(f64),
   169	    String(String),
   170	}
   171	
   172	/// To allow using expressions and literals in e.g. hashmaps, implement simple
   173	/// equality by value for all types, including Null and f64::NAN. This only
   174	/// checks that the values are the same, and ignores SQL semantics for e.g. NULL
   175	/// and NaN (which is handled by SQL expression evaluation).
   176	impl PartialEq for Literal {
   177	    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
   178	        match (self, other) {
   179	            (Self::Null, Self::Null) => true,
   180	            (Self::Boolean(l), Self::Boolean(r)) => l == r,
   181	            (Self::Integer(l), Self::Integer(r)) => l == r,
   182	            (Self::Float(l), Self::Float(r)) => l.to_bits() == r.to_bits(),
   183	            (Self::String(l), Self::String(r)) => l == r,
   184	            (_, _) => false,
   185	        }
   186	    }
   187	}
   188	
   189	impl Eq for Literal {}
   190	
   191	impl Hash for Literal {
   192	    fn hash<H: Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
   193	        core::mem::discriminant(self).hash(state);
   194	        match self {
   195	            Self::Null => {}
   196	            Self::Boolean(v) => v.hash(state),
   197	            Self::Integer(v) => v.hash(state),
   198	            Self::Float(v) => v.to_bits().hash(state),
   199	            Self::String(v) => v.hash(state),
   200	        }
   201	    }
   202	}

   204	/// Expression operators.
   205	///
   206	/// Since this is a recursive data structure, we have to box each child
   207	/// expression, which incurs a heap allocation. There are clever ways to get
   208	/// around this, but we keep it simple.
   209	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, Hash, PartialEq)]
   210	pub enum Operator {
   211	    And(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>), // a AND b
   212	    Not(Box<Expression>),                  // NOT a
   213	    Or(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),  // a OR b
   214	
   215	    Equal(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),       // a = b
   216	    GreaterThan(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>), // a > b
   217	    GreaterThanOrEqual(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>), // a >= b
   218	    Is(Box<Expression>, Literal),                  // IS NULL or IS NAN
   219	    LessThan(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),    // a < b
   220	    LessThanOrEqual(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>), // a <= b
   221	    NotEqual(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),    // a != b
   222	
   223	    Add(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),          // a + b
   224	    Divide(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),       // a / b
   225	    Exponentiate(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>), // a ^ b
   226	    Factorial(Box<Expression>),                     // a!
   227	    Identity(Box<Expression>),                      // +a
   228	    Multiply(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),     // a * b
   229	    Negate(Box<Expression>),                        // -a
   230	    Remainder(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),    // a % b
   231	    Subtract(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),     // a - b
   232	
   233	    Like(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>), // a LIKE b
   234	}

   236	impl Expression {
   237	    /// Walks the expression tree depth-first, calling a closure for every node.
   238	    /// Halts and returns false if the closure returns false.
   239	    pub fn walk(&self, visitor: &mut impl FnMut(&Expression) -> bool) -> bool {
   240	        use Operator::*;
   241	
   242	        if !visitor(self) {
   243	            return false;
   244	        }
   245	
   246	        match self {
   247	            Self::Operator(op) => match op {
   248	                Add(lhs, rhs)
   249	                | And(lhs, rhs)
   250	                | Divide(lhs, rhs)
   251	                | Equal(lhs, rhs)
   252	                | Exponentiate(lhs, rhs)
   253	                | GreaterThan(lhs, rhs)
   254	                | GreaterThanOrEqual(lhs, rhs)
   255	                | LessThan(lhs, rhs)
   256	                | LessThanOrEqual(lhs, rhs)
   257	                | Like(lhs, rhs)
   258	                | Multiply(lhs, rhs)
   259	                | NotEqual(lhs, rhs)
   260	                | Or(lhs, rhs)
   261	                | Remainder(lhs, rhs)
   262	                | Subtract(lhs, rhs) => lhs.walk(visitor) && rhs.walk(visitor),
   263	
   264	                Factorial(expr) | Identity(expr) | Is(expr, _) | Negate(expr) | Not(expr) => {
   265	                    expr.walk(visitor)
   266	                }
   267	            },
   268	
   269	            Self::Function(_, exprs) => exprs.iter().any(|expr| expr.walk(visitor)),
   270	
   271	            Self::All | Self::Column(_, _) | Self::Literal(_) => true,
   272	        }
   273	    }
   274	
   275	    /// Walks the expression tree depth-first while calling a closure until it
   276	    /// returns true. This is the inverse of walk().
   277	    pub fn contains(&self, visitor: &impl Fn(&Expression) -> bool) -> bool {
   278	        !self.walk(&mut |expr| !visitor(expr))
   279	    }
   280	
   281	    /// Find and collects expressions for which the given closure returns true,
   282	    /// adding them to c. Does not recurse into matching expressions.
   283	    pub fn collect(&self, visitor: &impl Fn(&Expression) -> bool, exprs: &mut Vec<Expression>) {
   284	        use Operator::*;
   285	
   286	        if visitor(self) {
   287	            exprs.push(self.clone());
   288	            return;
   289	        }
   290	
   291	        match self {
   292	            Self::Operator(op) => match op {
   293	                Add(lhs, rhs)
   294	                | And(lhs, rhs)
   295	                | Divide(lhs, rhs)
   296	                | Equal(lhs, rhs)
   297	                | Exponentiate(lhs, rhs)
   298	                | GreaterThan(lhs, rhs)
   299	                | GreaterThanOrEqual(lhs, rhs)
   300	                | LessThan(lhs, rhs)
   301	                | LessThanOrEqual(lhs, rhs)
   302	                | Like(lhs, rhs)
   303	                | Multiply(lhs, rhs)
   304	                | NotEqual(lhs, rhs)
   305	                | Or(lhs, rhs)
   306	                | Remainder(lhs, rhs)
   307	                | Subtract(lhs, rhs) => {
   308	                    lhs.collect(visitor, exprs);
   309	                    rhs.collect(visitor, exprs);
   310	                }
   311	                Factorial(expr) | Identity(expr) | Is(expr, _) | Negate(expr) | Not(expr) => {
   312	                    expr.collect(visitor, exprs);
   313	                }
   314	            },
   315	
   316	            Self::Function(_, args) => args.iter().for_each(|arg| arg.collect(visitor, exprs)),
   317	
   318	            Self::All | Self::Column(_, _) | Self::Literal(_) => {}
   319	        }
   320	    }
   321	}
